newsitem.title: USA: NYS Silver wants extra revenues to repay schools.
newsitem.headline: NYS Silver wants extra revenues to repay schools.

text.p: The New York State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, wants any extra windfall revenues the state collects to go towards repaying school aid owed to localities throughout the state.
The issue is particularly important for New York City, which is owed over $900 million, because for several years it failed to file the needed paperwork on time.

"One of the things we provide in the budget the Assembly passed is that any unanticipated revenues, such as the next budget surplus, shall be dedicated to paying off these obligations," Silver said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television on Thrsday.

The state Assembly, the Senate and Gov George Pataki have missed a March 10 deadline for agreeing on just how much New York State's tax revenues, which are riding high with Wall Street's profits, might exceed estimates in fiscal 1998.

No budget can be agreed until there is a consensus on how much money will be available to divide up, and the state, which last year set a national record by failing to agree on a budget until 104 days past its April 1 deadline, has again began a new fiscal year without a pact.
New York State ended fiscal 1997 with a $1.85 billion surplus.
